name: Melat Kiros
call_status: confirmed winner (AP called 3 Nov; ~78% vs R Christy Peterson ~14%, unaffiliated Shimon Blau ~6% in early returns)

bio.education: BA political science & economics, Washington College (MD); JD Univ. of Notre Dame (2022); doctoral student in public policy
bio.career: Former Sidley Austin associate (fired late 2023 after a Medium post on Gaza/pro-Palestine protests); PhD student and barista; first-time candidate

self_description: Democratic socialist and DSA member; defines democratic socialism as extending democratic rights and public services ('socialism already exists in public services like fire departments and schools'). Said she did not consider herself a socialist until after her campaign began.
primary_context: Defeated 15-term Rep. Diana DeGette (and Wanda James) on 30 June 2026 as a Justice Democrats / Denver DSA insurgent running on Medicare for All, abolish ICE and an Israel arms embargo; DeGette called her views 'really extreme'.

L1.e: Platform: 'Ultra-Millionaire Tax on net worth above $50 million' (2% annual) and 'corporate tax rate should be raised back above 50%'

L3.e: Medicare for All is a core plank; said 'single payer actually pays for itself' and called the ACA a 'band-aid'

L4.e: Self-identified democratic socialist / DSA member; platform backs 'publicly-owned, mixed-income social housing', repeal of Faircloth Amendment, and expanding publicly owned utilities on the TVA model

L5.e: Platform section 'Climate + Green New Deal': 'Investing in a Green New Deal that creates a just transition'; end fossil-fuel subsidies

L6.e: Called for breaking up big pharmaceutical companies (backs Break Up Big Medicine Act), data-center moratorium, 10% credit-card interest cap, ending at-will employment

L7.e: Trans Bill of Rights plank: 'Access to gender-affirming care for all ages, with medical decisions made by patients, families, and doctors, not politicians'

L9.e: Platform: 'We must Abolish ICE' and replace it with a humane immigration system

L12.e: Calls Israel's Gaza campaign a 'genocide' and supports 'an immediate and unconditional arms embargo on Israel'

C2.e: Calls ACA a 'band-aid'; supports single payer replacing private insurers

C3.e: Backs net-worth tax and corporate rate above 50%

C5.e: Per Colorado Politics, rejected several DSA platform planks including drastically reducing law enforcement (reporter's summary, not a direct quote)

EPD.note: No prior office; JD (Notre Dame) and BigLaw associate; 14-page platform naming specific bills/figures (Ultra-Millionaire Tax at $50M, Faircloth repeal, Break Up Big Medicine Act, PRO Act).

EO.note: Debated DeGette and James at LWV forum (May) and Colorado Politics/Denver Press Club forum (19 June). No general-election debate with Peterson/Blau found (Peterson did not engage with voter guide). Gave unscripted interviews incl. PBS Firing Line (Margaret Hoover), 9News, NOTUS, Denverite; on 9News/NOTUS declined to call Boulder firebombing antisemitic. Engages critics on substance (e.g. defended DSA-aligned policies, distanced herself from some DSA planks).

notable_positions: Medicare for All; 'single payer actually pays for itself' (https://thepostmillennial.com/ethiopian-dsa-colorado-congressional-hopeful-melat-kiros-says-us-to-blame-for-9-11-single-payer-healthcare-pays-for-itself-feds-should-fund-national-social-housing)
Abolish ICE; 'We will not wait to abolish ICE and pass Medicare for all' (https://kirosforco.com/priorities-2)
Immediate and unconditional arms embargo on Israel; calls Gaza a genocide (https://kirosforco.com/priorities-pdf-final.pdf)
2% annual tax on net worth above $50M; corporate rate above 50% (https://kirosforco.com/priorities-pdf-final.pdf)

Won't commit to backing Hakeem Jeffries for Speaker unless his agenda includes priorities like Medicare for All (https://www.denver7.com/news/politics/democracy-is-not-a-spectator-sport-cd1-democratic-nominee-melat-kiros-shares-policy-plans-if-elected)

Rejected DSA planks on abolishing the Senate, leaving NATO and drastically reducing law enforcement (https://www.coloradopolitics.com/2026/11/03/melat-kiros-shimon-blau-election-results-cd1-colorado/)
rationale: Kiros is a self-described democratic socialist backed by Justice Democrats, Denver DSA, Sanders, WFP and Sunrise, and her platform explicitly includes a wealth tax, Medicare for All, a Green New Deal, abolishing ICE, gender-affirming care for all ages and an Israel arms embargo. LI is well above 6. She has distanced herself from some DSA national planks (police, NATO, Senate), but that does not change the classification.

name: Eileen Laubacher
call_status: still uncalled by AP as of 9-10 Nov (Colorado Sun 9 Nov: AP had not called; Laubacher led by ~3,400 votes, ~49%-48%). CNN projected Laubacher on 9 Nov and she declared victory; Boebert has not conceded and her campaign signals a recount. Cure deadline 12 Nov, county counting ends 13 Nov; automatic recount if margin within 0.5% of winner's total (~930 votes). Treat as likely but unconfirmed.

bio.education: BS U.S. Naval Academy (1990); (further graduate degrees not confirmed)
bio.career: 34-year Navy career (intelligence officer, Afghanistan 2009, Rear Admiral 2018); Senior Defense Official/Defense Attache New Delhi 2019-22; Senior Director for South Asia, National Security Council (Biden); retired Oct 2024
bio.prior_office: none elected; flag officer (two-star rear admiral) and senior NSC staff

self_description: Former Republican who became unaffiliated, then a Democrat; says GOP no longer reflected her views on 'limited government and federal spending'; stresses 'service before self', working across party lines and rejecting 'loud, divisive voices on the fringes'.
primary_context: Effectively uncontested: rival Trisha Calvarese sued over Laubacher's short Democratic registration then dropped out before assembly; Laubacher beat write-in Jenna Preston on 30 June.

C3.e: Platform: 'Scrutinize the budget and make serious cuts to wasteful spending', middle-class tax cuts, backs balancing the budget; no wealth tax or rate hikes beyond ending breaks for data centers/corporations/billionaires

C4.e: Campaigns on 'Secure the border and remove dangerous criminals who are in the country illegally' alongside bipartisan reform

C5.e: Platform: 'Equip and train first responders and law enforcement, and invest in community policing'

C7.e: Former Republican; said in 12 Oct debate that a Democratic Congress should not impeach Trump; says rural America 'left behind by both parties'

C8.e: Backs 'all-of-the-above approach that includes clean, traditional, and alternative sources' of energy (while opposing federal land in CD4 as first option for extraction)

EPD.note: Flag officer (Rear Admiral) and NSC senior director = 3; USNA + senior national-security career = 2; platform has concrete items ($35 insulin cap, term/age limits, stock-trading ban, Farm Bill, water infrastructure) but few numbers or bill names = 1.

EO.note: Took part in the only scheduled televised debate with Boebert (9News/Kyle Clark, 12 Oct 2026) and answered questions on party switch, residency, Iran war and impeachment; answered Denver Post voter-guide Q&A and Colorado Water Congress appearance. No hostile-outlet interviews or regular town halls found.

notable_positions: Secure the border and remove dangerous criminals in the country illegally, plus bipartisan reform with path to citizenship (https://www.eileenforcolorado.com/platform)
'All-of-the-above' energy including traditional sources, but 'does not mean developing every available acre' (https://www.europesays.com/unitedstates/12789/)

Democrats should not impeach Trump if they win Congress (https://political.org/2026/10/13/rep-lauren-boebert-says-iran-war-has-been-detrimental-on-many-levels-in-debate-with-democrat-eileen-laubacher/)
Term limits and age limits for Congress; ban on members trading stocks (https://www.eileenforcolorado.com/platform)
Cut wasteful spending, balance the budget, middle-class tax cuts; end tax breaks for data centers (https://www.eileenforcolorado.com/platform)

Opposes Iran war: 'when negotiations are on the table, you do not start war' (https://political.org/2026/10/13/rep-lauren-boebert-says-iran-war-has-been-detrimental-on-many-levels-in-debate-with-democrat-eileen-laubacher/)
Victory statement: 'lower costs, protect healthcare, strengthen rural communities, take on corruption in both parties' (https://coloradosun.com/2026/11/09/lauren-boebert-vote-counting-update/)
rationale: A former Republican and retired rear admiral endorsed by the Blue Dog PAC, Laubacher campaigns on border security, deficit/spending cuts, all-of-the-above energy and against impeaching Trump; no left markers found (LI 0, CI about 7). Confidence is Medium because her platform is thin on contested issues (health-care model, trans issues, guns) and the race itself remains uncalled by AP.

outside_support: League of Conservation Voters Action Fund
Sens. Bennet, Hickenlooper, Slotkin, Kelly; Gov. Sherrill
notable_positions: Self-described 'middle-of-the-road centrist, almost center right, Democrat' (https://coloradosun.com/2025/07/15/jessica-killin-colorado-5th-congressional-district/)
Public option, not Medicare for All; reinstate ACA subsidies, repeal H.R.1 Medicaid cuts (https://coloradosun.com/2026/10/07/jeff-crank-jessica-killin-issue-guide-colorado/)
Supports 'common-sense work requirements' for able-bodied Medicaid adults (https://coloradosun.com/2026/10/07/jeff-crank-jessica-killin-issue-guide-colorado/)
Trump 'got it right' shutting the border, but deportations 'immoral and, in my mind, illegal' (https://coloradosun.com/2025/07/15/jessica-killin-colorado-5th-congressional-district/)
Make tips/overtime deductions permanent; roll back tax cuts for those over $1M; balance the budget (https://www.killinforcolorado.com/priorities)

name: Manny Rutinel
call_status: confirmed winner (campaign 'Statement From U.S. Representative-Elect Manny Rutinel on Victory in CO-08', 3 Nov; Wikipedia lists as member-elect defeating Gabe Evans)

bio.education: AA Pasco-Hernando State College; BA economics & BS microbiology Univ. of Florida; MS applied economics Johns Hopkins; JD Yale Law School
bio.career: Economist, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (2016-18); Earthjustice associate attorney; CEO of nonprofit Climate Refarm (2021-)
bio.prior_office: Colorado House of Representatives, HD-32 (appointed Oct 2023, elected 2024; resigned Sept 2026)

self_description: Frames himself around working families and 'facts and evidence'; says 'making progress requires working with others'. Campaign: 'Manny will work with anyone in Congress who wants to make healthcare affordable... whatever shape that takes.' On Gaza: 'I do not boil it down to one word descriptors.'
primary_context: Beat former state Rep. Shannon Bird (a self-styled bipartisan pragmatist) on 30 June 2026; the two agreed on almost every issue in debates. Colorado Sun reported that in a July 2025 Working Families Party endorsement interview he backed a fracking ban, single payer and student-debt cancellation, then reversed all three by May 2026; WFP did not endorse him.

L3.e: Now backs a public option 'If you like your private insurance, you're able to keep that', not Medicare for All (had backed single payer in a July 2025 WFP interview)

L5.e: Mixed: opposes a fracking ban now and backs 'all of the above' energy, but answered 'Yes' to a national moratorium on new oil and gas leases on federal land

L12.e: Supports continued U.S. military funding for Israel ('Israel is an ally'); declined to call Gaza a genocide ('I do not boil it down to one word descriptors')

C2.e: Backs a public option and restoring ACA credits, 'but not Medicare for All' (Colorado Sun, May 2026)

C5.e: Released 'Plan to Keep Our Communities Safe' calling for funding state and local law enforcement; endorsed by Adams County Sheriff Gene Claps

C8.e: 'I believe in an all-the-above energy approach'; opposes fracking ban; would streamline housing permitting

EPD.note: State legislator 2023-26 = 2; Yale JD + JHU MS + federal economist = 2; authored state legislation (18 prime-sponsored bills in first year; ICE detention oversight effort) = 2.

EO.note: Debated Bird in primary (Colorado Sun debate, 9News debate, UNC forum); accepted and attended 7 Oct general-election debate in Berthoud (The Surveyor) and a live-audience Colorado Sun interview with Evans. Media mostly mainstream/friendly (CPR, Denver Post, NYT). On substance, repeatedly declined to give positions when pressed: would not say if/when to stop fossil fuels, would not name tax cuts to reverse, no specifics on immigration, no one-word answer on Gaza; campaign did not explain his single-payer reversal.

notable_positions: Reversed July 2025 support for fracking ban, single payer and broad student-debt cancellation (https://coloradosun.com/2026/06/04/manny-rutinel-changed-positions-healthcare-student-debt-fracking/)
Public option alongside private insurance; restore ACA credits and Medicaid (https://coloradosun.com/2026/10/21/manny-rutinel-gabe-evans-voter-guide-colorado-district-8/)
Opposes Medicaid work requirements; lift the Social Security payroll-tax cap (https://coloradosun.com/2026/10/21/manny-rutinel-gabe-evans-voter-guide-colorado-district-8/)

ICE: judicial warrants and ID requirements rather than dismantling; led state lawmakers' call for ICE detention transparency (https://coloradosun.com/2026/05/28/manny-rutinel-shannon-bird-colorado-primary-issue-guide/)
Funding local police, securing southern border against fentanyl (https://www.mannyforcolorado.com/press)
Continued military aid to Israel with human-rights conditions; two-state solution (https://coloradosun.com/2026/10/21/manny-rutinel-gabe-evans-voter-guide-colorado-district-8/)
rationale: Rutinel's current stated positions are mainstream-to-centrist (public option not M4A, all-of-the-above energy, police funding, continued Israel aid) and he was New Dem-endorsed, but CI is only about 4 and he backed fracking ban/single payer as recently as July 2025. Well credentialed (Yale JD, state legislator) and debated, but often declined to state positions when pressed; the decision sequence lands on the nearest-of-1/4 fallback (imperfect fit), with Cat 3 a plausible alternative if his evasiveness is weighted more heavily.

name: Luke Bronin

bio.education: BA Yale; MSc Balliol College, Oxford (Rhodes Scholar); JD Yale Law School
bio.career: The Hartford (associate counsel, chief of staff to P&C division president); Navy Reserve intelligence officer (Afghanistan 2010-11, Lt.); Obama Treasury senior adviser and Deputy Assistant Secretary for Terrorist Financing; general counsel to Gov. L9.e: Issue page 'Abolishing ICE & Fixing Our Immigration System': 'Abolish ICE, which has only existed since 2003' and return enforcement to a broader-mission agency ('abolish and replace or rebuild ICE from the ground up')

C8.e: Climate page calls for building clean energy 'quickly and at scale... streamlining red tape that makes it too hard and costly to build'; housing page says 'we just don't build enough housing' and backs transit-oriented development and new financing tools

EO.note: Took part in NBC Connecticut televised forum (early July), WTNH News 8 debate (28 July) and a final debate (29 July) in the primary, engaging Larson directly on Social Security 2100 and defending his mayoral record. outside_support: Uniformed Professional Firefighters Association of CT
notable_positions: Abolish ICE in the longer term and return enforcement to a broader immigration agency; condition DHS funding on mask ban, warrants, ID (https://www.broninforcongress.com/issues/immigration)

'Strong public option so that any American who wants to participate in Medicare can'; 'push for universal, affordable healthcare' (https://www.broninforcongress.com/issues/protecting-medicare-medicaid-and-pushing-for-universal-healthcare)
Break up healthcare monopolies via Break Up Big Medicine Act (https://www.broninforcongress.com/issues/protecting-medicare-medicaid-and-pushing-for-universal-healthcare)
Build more housing and clean energy fast by cutting red tape (https://www.broninforcongress.com/issues/building-more-housing)
Assault weapons ban, universal background checks, red-flag laws (https://www.broninforcongress.com/issues)
AI regulation a top priority from campaign launch (https://ctmirror.org/2026/10/20/after-larsons-loss-cts-1st-district-will-elect-a-new-member/)
